title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
abstract: arXiv:2610.22300v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Not all facts a language model can recall support further learning equally well. We distinguish active facts, which support generalization beyond their own recall, from inert facts, which can be recalled but do not support such generalization in a given task. We study this distinction by constructing new relations from existing ones. Take the relation that maps a place to its continent (Paris -> Europe) and assign each of its answers an arbitrary new label (Europe -> crab, Asia -> zebra). The new relation then maps Paris -> crab. We fine-tune the model on the new relation for a subset of subjects, without telling it the original relation or the relabeling rule, and test whether it assigns the corresponding labels to held-out subjects that share an answer in the original relation. Having learned Paris -> crab, does it answer Munich -> crab? Across eleven language models and 70 relations, how linearly readable the original relation is in

translated_title: 微调前呈线性的知识在微调后能够泛化
translated_abstract: 并非语言模型能够回忆的所有事实都能同样好地支持进一步的学习。我们区分了“活性事实”与“惰性事实”：前者能够支持超出其自身回忆范围的泛化，后者虽然可以被回忆起来，但在给定任务中却不支持这种泛化。我们通过从已有关系构造新关系的方式来研究这一区分。以将地点映射到其所属大洲的关系（巴黎 → 欧洲）为例，为每个答案分配一个任意的新标签（欧洲 → 螃蟹，亚洲 → 斑马），于是新关系便将巴黎映射为螃蟹。我们在一部分主体上用新关系对模型进行微调，但不告诉模型原始关系或重新标注规则，然后测试模型能否为那些在原始关系中共享相同答案的留出主体分配相应的标签。也就是说，在学会了“巴黎 → 螃蟹”之后，模型能否回答出“慕尼黑 → 螃蟹”？在十一个语言模型和七十个关系的实验中，原始关系的线性可读程度……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 论文提出区分语言模型中支持泛化的“活性事实”与仅可回忆的“惰性事实”，并通过重标注实验发现：微调前在模型内部呈线性可读的知识，在微调后能够泛化到共享相同答案的未训练实体上。
en_tdlr: Distinguishing "active facts" from "inert facts" via a relabeling experiment, the paper shows that knowledge that is linearly readable in a language model before fine-tuning generalizes to held-out entities sharing the same answer after fine-tuning.
